log.what: Asked q3 at 0x41f881: zooRatingUpdate averages entity+0x2a8 for guests (the 0x638700 branch, with the needs thresholds) as it does for animals' happiness, but 5 guests read ~230 on average live (Jan 20, Year 1) - not -100..100. log.by: batty251
batty251
log.what: Asked q4 at 0x41f881: The original pauses with 'The National Organization of Zoos has received numerous complaints... you will not be able to adopt any new animals' when a lone zebra's happiness reached about -60 (Feb 1, Year 1). Our engine has no such ban. Where's the rule (its threshold, and what lifts it)? re/msg.py didn't find the text by 'National Organization'.

log.by: batty251
log.what: Answered q4: It isn't in zoo.exe: it's freeform/donation.scn's [loseadopt] goal (rulea=1 ruleb=0: animals' average happiness on the 0-100 scale, (h+100)/2; type=1 value=25: below 25) firing trulea=2 truleb=12 targa=1 targb=20 - disable [1]'s id=2075 and 2080 (the adopt buttons) and show popup [20] (lang0.dll TEXT SCN11_NOBUY_ANIMALS, pause=1). [canadopt] (average above 45) and [canadopt2] (no animals) enable them again with popup [21] (SCN11_CANBUY_ANIMALS). Our game's goals (main.cpp setupGoals) already did this; the Lab's Test Zoo didn't load goals at all - it does now (Lab.cpp setupGoals), and fired the same ban, message and pause at an average of -52.

log.by: batty251
log.what: Answered q3: My misreading: the Lab readout summed each class's +0x2a8 and I took the sum (5 guests, 230) for an average. Read one by one (Feb 1, Year 1) guests' +0x2a8 runs 15..50 in steps of 5, oldest lowest - happiness on -100..100, a new guest starting at 50 (as in our engine). So +0x2a8 is happiness for guests as for animals.

log.by: batty251 (checked StevenGann's findings against the shipped maps and zoo.exe)
log.what: Lead q8 at 0x4c25cf: ambient's blob is shaped differently from every other category. The 28-byte prefix is right in spirit but its fields do not line up at +0x04/+0x08/+0x10, and reading +0x08/+0x0C/+0x14 does not fix it either - so an offset inside an ambient blob should be treated as unverified. Evidence: only ambient has negative y (5 records across 94 maps - crows, seagulls, birds; y -7 to -39, i.e. just above the map's top edge, with a sane x), and only ambient has values at +0x10 that are not directions (multiples of 16, -192..192). So StevenGann's 'negative means not placed' and 'direction is only 0/2/4/6' both hold for ordinary categories and fail for ambient.

questions.answer: They're happiness's floor and ceiling: -100 and 100, set in ZTAnimalType's defaults (code at 0x4b659e, no Ghidra function: +0x228 = 60, +0x22c = -100, +0x230 = 100) - no config key reads them, which is why the key map missed them. animalUpdateHappiness raises +0x2a8 to species[0x8b] and caps it at [0x8c]. Found with the Lab's field:0x22c search (the write 'mov [ebp+0x22c], 0xffffff9c' beside the loaders). Saved as ZTAnimalType.minHappiness / maxHappiness.

Two aren't starts and stay as they are: 0x4375d3 is a piece of a bigger function (it compares 'bSleep'/'bHatch', jumps back to 0x43721c and returns through that one's frame), and 0x58fbf0 is a jump table (pointers into 0x58fbxx) just before the research-effect code - the engine's comments can cite them, but there's no function to make.

questions.answer: My misreading: the Lab readout summed each class's +0x2a8 and I took the sum (5 guests, 230) for an average. Read one by one (Feb 1, Year 1) guests' +0x2a8 runs 15..50 in steps of 5, oldest lowest - happiness on -100..100, a new guest starting at 50 (as in our engine). So +0x2a8 is happiness for guests as for animals.
questions.question: zooRatingUpdate averages entity+0x2a8 for guests (the 0x638700 branch, with the needs thresholds) as it does for animals' happiness, but 5 guests read ~230 on average live (Jan 20, Year 1) - not -100..100. Is guests' +0x2a8 happiness on another scale, or another field?

questions.answer: It isn't in zoo.exe: it's freeform/donation.scn's [loseadopt] goal (rulea=1 ruleb=0: animals' average happiness on the 0-100 scale, (h+100)/2; type=1 value=25: below 25) firing trulea=2 truleb=12 targa=1 targb=20 - disable [1]'s id=2075 and 2080 (the adopt buttons) and show popup [20] (lang0.dll TEXT SCN11_NOBUY_ANIMALS, pause=1). [canadopt] (average above 45) and [canadopt2] (no animals) enable them again with popup [21] (SCN11_CANBUY_ANIMALS). Our game's goals (main.cpp setupGoals) already did this; the Lab's Test Zoo didn't load goals at all - it does now (Lab.cpp setupGoals), and fired the same ban, message and pause at an average of -52.
questions.question: The original pauses with 'The National Organization of Zoos has received numerous complaints... you will not be able to adopt any new animals' when a lone zebra's happiness reached about -60 (Feb 1, Year 1). Our engine has no such ban. Where's the rule (its threshold, and what lifts it)? re/msg.py didn't find the text by 'National Organization'.

questions.by: batty251 (checked StevenGann's findings against the shipped maps and zoo.exe)
questions.question: StevenGann's independent .zoo findings: (a) entity record = 3 x (u32 len + bytes) = [category, name, code], then u32 blob_len + blob; (b) x = i32 @ blob+0x04 / 64, y = i32 @ blob+0x08 / 64, tile = y*width + x. Verified here 2026-10-14 by parsing 94 shipped .zoo files / 95,951 records with rule (a): zero structural failures, v70-v106 including expansions; and rule (b): 95,950 of 95,951 coordinates land on the map grid. Worth folding into the reader docs.
